notes: EBIT proxy is AMETEK consolidated operating income (recorded as 'Operating income' in the 10-K segment reconciliation). ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1037868/000103786826000016/ame-20251231.htm))

D&A equals 'Depreciation and amortization' from the consolidated statement of cash flows; capex equals 'Additions to property, plant and equipment'. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1037868/000103786826000016/ame-20251231.htm))

NWC definition used for construction is (Receivables + Inventories + Other current assets) − (Accounts payable + Customer advanced payments + Income taxes payable + Accrued liabilities and other), excluding cash and short-term debt. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1037868/000103786826000016/ame-20251231.htm))

Investments in the assumptions are proxied using the 10-K 'Investments and other assets' line as a non-operating add-back proxy; this may include items not purely discretionary cash equivalents. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1037868/000103786826000016/ame-20251231.htm))

NOL balance is modeled using the 10-K disclosure of tax-effected benefits related to NOL carryforwards (not gross NOL). Utilization is an assumption (0.80) due to lack of specific utilization schedule disclosure. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1037868/000103786826000016/ame-20251231.htm))
WACC and tax_rate are market-data estimates from StockAnalysis (not directly disclosed by AMETEK). ([stockanalysis.com](https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/ame/statistics/))

catalysts: Further beats/raises to FY2026 mid-to-high single digit sales trajectory and EPS progression as backlog converts. ([ametek.com](https://www.ametek.com/newsroom/news/investor/2026/february/ametek-announces-record-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-results))

Margin expansion opportunities from operational excellence and integration of recent acquisitions (especially where dilution/integration costs normalize). ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1037868/000103786826000016/ame-20251231.htm))

Continued capital allocation (buybacks/dividends) supported by strong operating cash flow and conversion. ([ametek.com](https://www.ametek.com/newsroom/news/investor/2026/february/ametek-announces-record-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-results))
company_overview: AMETEK is a global provider of industrial technology solutions operating through two reportable segments: Electronic Instruments Group (EIG) and Electromechanical Group (EMG). ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1037868/000103786826000016/ame-20251231.htm))

In FY2025, AMETEK reported net sales of 7,401,116,000 and consolidated operating income of 1,910,317,000 (25.8% of net sales). ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1037868/000103786826000016/ame-20251231.htm))

The company’s model emphasizes operational excellence, technology innovation, global/market expansion, and strategic acquisitions. ([ametek.com](https://www.ametek.com/newsroom/news/investor/2026/february/ametek-announces-record-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-results))
current_context: Management guided FY2026 overall sales to be up mid-to-high single digits vs. FY2025. ([ametek.com](https://www.ametek.com/newsroom/news/investor/2026/february/ametek-announces-record-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-results))

For 1Q 2026, overall sales were expected to be up approximately 10% year-over-year at the midpoint. ([ametek.com](https://www.ametek.com/newsroom/news/investor/2026/february/ametek-announces-record-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-results))
FY2026 capital expenditures are expected to be approximately 2% of net sales. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1037868/000103786826000016/ame-20251231.htm))
investment_highlights: Base-case revenue growth ramps down from mid-to-high single digits in 2026 toward a mature mid-single digit profile by 2030, consistent with the company’s FY2026 guidance and historical execution. ([ametek.com](https://www.ametek.com/newsroom/news/investor/2026/february/ametek-announces-record-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-results))

EBIT margin is modeled to stay in a tight range near historical levels (~25.6%–26.2%), reflecting core margin durability despite acquisition integration effects. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1037868/000103786826000016/ame-20251231.htm))

Capital intensity remains controlled (capex modeled at ~1.9% of sales), aligning with stated ~2% capex expectations for 2026. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1037868/000103786826000016/ame-20251231.htm))

Working capital is modeled using a net working capital framework calibrated to the last three year-end balance sheets, resulting in NWC at ~0.12–0.124 of sales in the forecast. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1037868/000103786825000012/ame-20241231.htm))
key_risks: End-market cyclicality and sales-mix shifts could pressure organic growth and/or EBIT margin outside the base-case range. ([ametek.com](https://www.ametek.com/newsroom/news/investor/2026/february/ametek-announces-record-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-results))
Acquisition execution risk: continued margin dilution or weaker-than-expected synergy capture. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1037868/000103786826000016/ame-20251231.htm))

Working capital swings (modeled near ~0.12–0.124 of sales) could reduce free cash flow if tied to higher receivables/inventories than assumed. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1037868/000103786826000016/ame-20251231.htm))

presentation.subtitle: AMETEK (AME) DCF & Comps Valuation Inputs — March 2026
valuation_summary: DCF inputs use an equity/credit-style discount rate (WACC) and tax rate consistent with available market-data estimates, with terminal value driven by long-run growth (2.5%) and a peer-anchored exit EV/EBITDA. ([stockanalysis.com](https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/ame/statistics/))

The selected terminal exit multiple (20.0x) is positioned within the observed industrial/automation peer EV/EBITDA band (roughly ~14.5x to ~24.4x) from the comps set. ([stockanalysis.com](https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/ftv/statistics/?utm_source=openai))

Comps are included to sanity-check implied valuation levels relative to forward earnings expectations (Forward P/E) and enterprise-value scaling (EV/Revenue, EV/EBITDA). ([stockanalysis.com](https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/ftv/statistics/?utm_source=openai))
